findings.title: The warning calls POST and PATCH "an unsafe method", but the check flags non-idempotent methods, and PUT and DELETE are unsafe too yet never reported.
findings.problem: RFC 9110 defines safe (section 9.2.1: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE) and idempotent (section 9.2.2, which adds PUT and DELETE) as different properties, and the check decides on the second. A user who knows the RFC reads the warning as "retrylint flags retries on unsafe methods" and expects a warning for a retried PUT or DELETE that never comes; one who does not learns a rule that contradicts the README. Rewording this warning is the whole change, so the reason it now prints is a claim the code does not keep.

evidence.text: retrylint/messages.py:6: `f"{file}:{endpoint.line}: {endpoint.method} {endpoint.path} => retry x{endpoint.retries} on an unsafe method; "`

retrylint/__main__.py:7-9: `# RFC 9110, section 9.2.2 defines GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT, and DELETE as idempotent.` and `IDEMPOTENT = {"GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "TRACE", "PUT", "DELETE"}`; line 16 warns when `endpoint.method not in IDEMPOTENT`. The function is named `non_idempotent_retry` (messages.py:4).

README.md:19-20: "it is only harmless for a method that RFC 9110 defines as idempotent (section 9.2.2): GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT, and DELETE. POST and PATCH are not idempotent." README.md has no "unsafe".
Base text: "but {endpoint.method} is not idempotent (RFC 9110, section 9.2.2)".

Ran the head on `PUT /orders/42 5`, `POST /orders 3`, `DELETE /x 1`, `CONNECT /t 2`, `POST /y 1`: lines 2, 4, and 5 are reported, each "... on an unsafe method; ..."; PUT and DELETE are not. tests/golden/put_delete_retry.txt is empty for retried PUT and DELETE.
RFC 9110 section 9.2.1 lists only GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE as safe, so PUT and DELETE are unsafe methods.

findings.proposed_solution:
Update tests/golden/post_retry.txt and tests/golden/patch_retry.txt to match. For tests/golden/post_retry.conf the user then sees:

tests/golden/post_retry.conf:3: POST /orders => retry x3 on a non-idempotent method; a retry may apply its effect twice. Drop the retry policy.

reproducer.code:
printf 'PUT /orders/42 5\nPOST /orders 3\n' > mix.conf
python3 -m retrylint mix.conf
# current:  mix.conf:2: POST /orders => retry x3 on an unsafe method; ...   (PUT, also unsafe, is not reported)
# expected: the reason names non-idempotence, the property that separates POST from PUT

findings.suggestion: f"{file}:{endpoint.line}: {endpoint.method} {endpoint.path} => retry x{endpoint.retries} on a non-idempotent method; "
findings.retest: The warnings for `POST /orders 3` and `PATCH /orders/42 2` (tests/golden/post_retry.txt, patch_retry.txt) say the method is not idempotent and contain no "unsafe" or "safe"; the same holds for `CONNECT /t 2`, a method outside IDEMPOTENT that the check also flags (at the head it prints "on an unsafe method"); `PUT /orders/42 5` still gets no warning.

findings.title: "Drop the retry policy" tells the user to remove the client's whole policy, where what clears the warning is setting this endpoint's retries to 0.
findings.problem: The README calls the whole file, which lists every endpoint, the retry policy of the client, so a user who follows the advice removes the retries of GET and PUT endpoints the tool accepts too, and the advice names no setting the user can find in the file.

evidence.text: retrylint/messages.py:7: `f"a retry may apply its effect twice. Drop the retry policy."`
README.md:3-4: "`retrylint` checks the retry policy of an HTTP client before it ships. A policy file lists one endpoint per line"; retrylint/policy.py:1: "Reads a retry policy file."
retrylint/__main__.py:16 warns only when `endpoint.retries > 0`; tests/golden/patch_retry.conf:2 `POST /payments 0` gets no warning.
Base text: "Remove the retry, or send an Idempotency-Key header that the server deduplicates."

The tool cannot see request headers, so it keeps warning on a POST that sends an Idempotency-Key; setting the retries to 0 is the only remedy that clears the warning. Whether to name the key as well is the author's decision that F4 asks about.

findings.proposed_solution:
Update the two golden files to match. For tests/golden/post_retry.conf the user then sees:

tests/golden/post_retry.conf:3: POST /orders => retry x3 on an unsafe method; a retry may apply its effect twice. Set the endpoint's retries to 0.
findings.suggestion: f"a retry may apply its effect twice. Set the endpoint's retries to 0."
findings.retest: The advice in the warnings for `POST /orders 3` and `PATCH /orders/42 2` names that endpoint's retries (the `retries` column) and a value that passes the check, such as 0, and does not say "the retry policy".

findings.title: `=> retry x3` replaces "is retried up to 3 times" with notation no user can look up, and no longer says whether 3 counts retries or attempts.
findings.problem: HTTP client libraries count this both ways, so `retry x3` reads as three sends or four, while the policy file's column counts retries after the first attempt (README.md:4). `=>` reads as "maps to", "leads to", or "is configured as". The plain wording keeps the endpoint and the count first, as the commit asks.

evidence.text: tests/golden/post_retry.txt:1: "tests/golden/post_retry.conf:3: POST /orders => retry x3 on an unsafe method; ..."; base: `endpoint "POST /orders" is retried up to 3 times`.
README.md:4: the third column is "how many times the client retries a failed request".
No other output text, README line, or comment in the repository uses `=>` or an `xN` count.

findings.proposed_solution:
Write the count in words, after the endpoint, with "time" for a count of 1. With F1's term worded as a clause, the POST line reads:

tests/golden/post_retry.conf:3: POST /orders is retried up to 3 times, but POST is not idempotent; a retry may apply its effect twice. Drop the retry policy.

and a line with one retry reads `client.conf:5: POST /y is retried up to 1 time, but POST is not idempotent; ...`. With F2 applied as well, the POST line ends "Set the endpoint's retries to 0." (167 characters).
findings.retest: The warnings in tests/golden/post_retry.txt and patch_retry.txt contain no `=>` and no `x<digits>` and state the count as retries in words; a policy line with 1 retry, such as `POST /y 1` (at the head `POST /y => retry x1`), renders a grammatical singular.

findings.title: The commit message describes a shortening and a reordering, but the change also drops the Idempotency-Key remedy and the RFC 9110 section 9.2.2 reference from the warning, and says neither.
findings.problem: A reader of `git log` concludes that the warning still says the same thing in fewer words, and a reviewer cannot tell whether dropping the second remedy was a decision or a side effect of the cut.

evidence.text: Commit body: "The warning wrapped over three lines in an 80-column terminal, and the endpoint and the retry count sat in the middle of it. Put them first and keep the message short enough to scan in a CI log." Nothing else describes a change of content.

Removed (base retrylint/messages.py): "is not idempotent (RFC 9110, section 9.2.2)" and "Remove the retry, or send an Idempotency-Key header that the server deduplicates." Added, retrylint/messages.py:6-7: "on an unsafe method;" and "Drop the retry policy."

findings.proposed_solution: Restore the dropped content in the short form, or say in the commit body that the warning no longer suggests an Idempotency-Key header and no longer cites RFC 9110, and why. The changed reason ("unsafe method") is F1's; once F1 is fixed, the body need not mention it.

reproducer.code:
git log -1 --format=%B 7463fb4 | grep -Ei 'idempotency-key|idempotent|rfc'
# current: no output; expected: the message names each dropped piece of content, or the warning keeps it

findings.retest: Each piece of content the old warning had and the new one lacks (the Idempotency-Key remedy, the RFC 9110 section 9.2.2 reference) is either stated in the commit message or present in the warning again.

findings.title: Is the shortened warning meant to fit one 80-column line? Every warning still wraps, and no test bounds its length.
findings.problem: The commit gives the 80-column wrap as the reason for the change. The fixed text alone is 91 characters before the file, line, method, and path are added, so no input fits one 80-column line, and the fixes F1-F3 propose make it longer. Nothing stops a later edit from lengthening it again.

evidence.text: tests/golden/post_retry.txt:1 is 136 characters and tests/golden/patch_retry.txt:1 is 141; `fold -w 80` splits each into 2 lines (the base lines were 303 and 309 characters, 4 lines each).

The literal parts of retrylint/messages.py:6-7, " => retry x on an unsafe method; a retry may apply its effect twice. Drop the retry policy.", are 91 characters; the warning for `a.conf`, `POST /x 3` is 109.
tests/test_golden.py:20 compares the whole output with the golden file; no test asserts a line length.
The commit body states no length of its own; reading it as one 80-column line per warning is an inference.

reproducer.code:
def test_warning_for_a_short_path_fits_one_80_column_line(self):
    warning = messages.non_idempotent_retry("a.conf", Endpoint(1, "POST", "/x", 3))
    self.assertLessEqual(len(warning), 80, warning)
    # current: AssertionError: 109 not less than or equal to 80
    # expected: passes, if one 80-column line is the target

findings.retest: Settled by the author's answer: where the target is one 80-column line for a short path, a test such as the reproducer exists, fails at the reviewed head, and passes with the new wording; where it is not, the commit message states the target the change keeps (for example, shorter than before, endpoint and count first) and no test is owed.

findings.title: The commit message says the old warning wrapped over three lines in an 80-column terminal; it wrapped over four.

evidence.text: The base first lines of tests/golden/post_retry.txt and tests/golden/patch_retry.txt are 303 and 309 characters; `fold -w 80` splits each into 4 lines.

reproducer.code:
git show 8587e48:tests/golden/post_retry.txt | head -1 | fold -w 80 | wc -l
# current: 4; the commit message says three

findings.retest: The line count or length the commit message states for the old warning matches `git show 8587e48:tests/golden/post_retry.txt | head -1 | fold -w 80 | wc -l`.

classes.title: The shortened warning swaps the field's words for shorthand
classes.root_cause: The rewrite of non_idempotent_retry cut length by replacing the RFC term, the retry count wording, and the remedy with shorthand ("unsafe method", "=> retry xN", "the retry policy") that says something other than what the check decides.
